pages.observations: Lecture 49 title and institutional attribution, printed 1; no technical content.
Contents roadmap, printed 2; ten listed topics are developed later.
ASR ear versus conversational brain; words versus intent. Explicit phoneme decomposition is overgeneralized if treated as universal.
Five-node timeline from ELIZA to ChatGPT; ALICE labeled retrieval and context memory. Broad chronology, not exact invention dating.
Hidden human and AI exchange text with judge; behavioral indistinguishability does not establish internal understanding or emotion.
Weather request and answer diagram; chatbot communication layer and channel/implementation distinction.
IF hello rule and rule-found diamond; NO reaches fallback. Predictability/fixed tasks contrasted with unseen-input limitations; broad statelessness claim needs qualification.
Reusable ELIZA engine and replaceable scripts; cat dialogue reflects I as you; memory claim conflicts with original limited MEMORY mechanism.
Six vertical boxes: tokenize, standardize, keywords, decomposition, reassembly, postprocess. Callouts include file-order priority and random template selection; original ranks and cycling differ.
Five vector-retrieval boxes; semantic proximity and fixed-bank limitation. No numeric cosine values are printed.
ALICE title literally says Linguist; primary nomenclature says Linguistic. Authored patterns, larger phrase database and open-source architecture are described.
AIML expands to Artificial Intelligence Markup Language; XML structure and four tag roles, including hidden think evaluation.
Exact I PLAY wildcard, empty person inside set_it; transformed possessive is both retained and returned under supplied legacy semantics.
Exact I READ wildcard BOOKS; nested topic/does/it setters and separate personality setter are inside think. Visible request remains; safety claim is overbroad.
Generative responses proceed token by token; available context conditions prediction. Most probable wording describes greedy choice, not all sampling policies.

Literal Python imports and loaders, absent model_id/question assignments, three-newline prompt, pipeline lookup and top-level return. Caption calls excerpt simplified; linked original remains unavailable under denial.
Sequential ASR–LLM–TTS chain, local and remote examples, and loss/latency/error limitations. Ollama runtime is distinct from Llama model.
Commercial-assistant statements are bulleted, NOT numbered. Wake, captured request, NLP, action/response and TTS; broad product capabilities are source-scoped.
Resource constraints motivate local wake-word stage followed by local or cloud ASR. Listening/activated panels show Hello robot; transient acquisition is not persistent recording.
Yellow STT→Intent Parsing→LLM path then blue TTS and ROS→Action branches. Prose says immediate/instant but the drawing alone guarantees neither timing nor safe motion.
Three utterance bubbles converge on cleanup program; those needs contextual grounding and routine scope remains bounded.
Two exact keyword reductions are pick toys and clean room; diagram strikes out up as well. Negation/reference loss can undermine the general accuracy claim.
Three limitations separate missing paralinguistics, serial latency and propagated errors; direct SpeechLM need not use a mandatory plain-text bottleneck.
Tokenizer, LM and vocoder; speech and text rows have cross-modal paths, not a compulsory ASR stage. Captioned fox prefix continues as lazy dog.
Semantic/acoustic token trade-off and mixed approach; duplex requires listening while speaking, interruption handling and appropriate silence. Tokens alone do not establish these guarantees.
What versus how includes pitch/rhythm/intonation; internal state is unobserved, not uninferable. Adaptive personality is simulated behavior, not proof of feeling.
Third-person external facial/vocal cues, fallible multimodal pattern recognition and emotion-engine motivation. No operational proof of inner experience.
Summary repeats rules/retrieval/generation, intent/context, direct speech, duplex and affective-cue themes; no unique new examinable angle.
Two references: Govers book and Cui et al. SpeechLM survey; bibliographic page only.
